MK: In pediatrics, based on the child’s underlying condition it may be possible to select some resuscitative interventions (like intubation or cardioversion) and not others (like chest compressions). It is very rare, however, to elect for chest compressions without intubation—this would not be recommended as it is very unlikely to be successful.
ICS: Don’t forget to ask permission to discuss a very difficult topic.
“There’s something I’d like to talk with you about – it’s something I ask all of my patients when they are first admitted to the hospital, no matter how healthy they are.”
“It’s about something called code status, which provides direction to the medical teams about what patients may or may not want done should their heart stop beating or should they stop breathing.”

“If a patient’s heart stops beating, we sometimes press firmly on their chest to pump blood through their body, use electricity to shock their heart back into beating, and place a breathing tube in their windpipe.”
“I can understand how this would be confusing and I don’t think it’s likely to happen. Some of my patients have strong opinions on this topic and I ask because it’s important I honor their wishes.”

*Example response:* It is important to acknowledge the emotion and ask permission to continue the discussion. For example, “I can tell this discussion is causing you some anxiety/stress/fear. Discussing code status is difficult. Is it ok if we continue with the discussion, or would you like to have this discussion at a different time?”
